## 08 Movies about advertising

Films and series about advertising, persuasion, brands and the people who sell them. Year, director and what each one is really about.

### Thank You for Smoking (2005)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/thank-you-for-smoking/
Date: 2026-09-05. Read: 2 min.

Jason Reitman's satire follows a tobacco lobbyist who can argue any side. A film about spin, and about the difference between persuasion and truth.

Based on Christopher Buckley's 1994 novel. Aaron Eckhart plays Nick Naylor, whose job is to make the indefensible sound reasonable, and who is very good company while he does it. That is the uncomfortable part. Technique works whether or not the claim underneath it is true.

### The Founder (2016)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/the-founder/
Date: 2026-09-01. Read: 2 min.

Ray Kroc turns a single hamburger stand into McDonald's. The product was the brothers'. The brand, the system and the name became his.

Directed by John Lee Hancock, with Michael Keaton as Kroc. Watch it for one question: what is left of a brand once you separate it from the people who made the product. The film's answer is a name, a set of standards, and the right to sell both.

### Art & Copy (2009)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/art-and-copy/
Date: 2026-08-28. Read: 2 min.

Doug Pray's documentary on the creative revolution in advertising, with Lee Clow, George Lois, Mary Wells Lawrence, Hal Riney and others on the work that defined the trade.

The film covers Volkswagen's Think Small, Apple's 1984 and Nike's Just Do It, told by the people who made them. It is the clearest record on film of how the modern agency creative department came to be, and the best case we have seen for why it was worth paying for.

### The Greatest Movie Ever Sold (2011)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/the-greatest-movie-ever-sold/
Date: 2026-08-22. Read: 2 min.

Morgan Spurlock makes a documentary about product placement, funded entirely by product placement. The pitch meetings are the film.

Every sponsor deal, every brand integration and every compromise is on camera. The film shows how brand money shapes content by letting brand money shape it, which is either very honest or very convenient.

### The Century of the Self (2002)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/the-century-of-the-self/
Date: 2026-08-17. Read: 3 min.

Adam Curtis's four-part BBC series on Edward Bernays and how ideas from psychoanalysis were used to shape public relations, advertising and consumer culture.

Bernays, a nephew of Sigmund Freud, is presented as the link between the unconscious and the business of persuasion. Curtis argues a case rather than reporting one, which is worth knowing going in. It is still the historical backbone of the Branding section, a century before the scanners.

### How to Get Ahead in Advertising (1989)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/how-to-get-ahead-in-advertising/
Date: 2026-08-11. Read: 2 min.

Bruce Robinson's comedy about an ad executive whose crisis of conscience grows into a talking boil that wants his job.

Richard E. Grant plays Denis Bagley, who cannot finish a campaign for a pimple cream. The film is a satire of the trade from the inside, and one of the few that takes the question of whether advertising is honest work seriously.

### The Joneses (2009)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/the-joneses/
Date: 2026-08-05. Read: 2 min.

A perfect family moves into a wealthy suburb. They are not a family. They are a stealth marketing unit, and everything they own is for sale.

Derrick Borte's film, with David Duchovny and Demi Moore, got to influencer marketing before the word was common. The neighbours do not buy the products. They buy the life the products are standing in for.

### Mad Men (2007 to 2015)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/mad-men/
Date: 2026-07-30. Read: 3 min.

Seven seasons of Madison Avenue in the 1960s. The Carousel pitch in the first season is still the best short explanation of what a brand sells.

Matthew Weiner's series follows Don Draper and the agency Sterling Cooper through the decade. The period detail is what people remember. What the show argues, across seven seasons, is that advertising sells the buyer a feeling about themselves rather than a fact about the product.

### Putney Swope (1969)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/movies-about-advertising/putney-swope/
Date: 2026-07-24. Read: 2 min.

Robert Downey Sr.'s satire: the token Black executive at a Madison Avenue agency is accidentally elected chairman and turns the place upside down.

The film is uneven and deliberately so. It survives because its fake commercials are still funnier and sharper than most real ones.

## 09 Songs

Songs that are about advertising, selling, media and wanting things. Not songs used in ads. Songs about the business of it.

### This Note's for You. Neil Young (1988)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/this-notes-for-you/
Date: 2026-09-06. Read: 2 min.

A refusal to sell songs to sponsors, with a title that parodies a beer slogan. MTV initially declined to air the video, then gave it Video of the Year in 1989.

The lyric names the brands it will not sing for. The video parodied the celebrity endorsements everyone else was taking. As a statement of the artist's side of the sponsorship bargain, nothing has beaten it since.

### Sell Out. Reel Big Fish (1996)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/sell-out/
Date: 2026-09-02. Read: 2 min.

A ska-punk band signs to a major label and writes a hit about signing to a major label. The commercial bargain, sung from inside it.

The song knows exactly what it is: the product of the deal it is mocking. That tension is the whole subject of this section, and this song says it out loud.

### Television, the Drug of the Nation. The Disposable Heroes of Hiphoprisy (1992)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/television-the-drug-of-the-nation/
Date: 2026-08-27. Read: 2 min.

Michael Franti's spoken-word indictment of broadcast media, consumption and attention, written before the feed replaced the channel.

Every line about television reads today as a line about the phone. That it has not dated is a verdict on us, not a compliment to Franti.

### Money. Pink Floyd (1973)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/money/
Date: 2026-08-21. Read: 2 min.

Cash registers as percussion, a 7/4 riff, and a lyric about the economy of wanting. From The Dark Side of the Moon.

The song became a hit single, which the band found ironic. It sits in this list because wanting is the raw material every marketer works with.

### Material Girl. Madonna (1984)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/material-girl/
Date: 2026-08-15. Read: 2 min.

Consumer desire as identity, delivered as pop. The video restages Marilyn Monroe's Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend.

Madonna has said the song was meant ironically. It became a label anyway, which is the part worth sitting with. The market decided what the brand stood for and did not ask.

### Advertising Space. Robbie Williams (2005)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/advertising-space/
Date: 2026-08-09. Read: 2 min.

A ballad about Elvis Presley and what fame does to a person once the image becomes inventory.

The title is the thesis. A star's face, name and story become surfaces to sell on. The song is about the cost, sung by someone who knew it.

### Don't Believe the Hype. Public Enemy (1988)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/dont-believe-the-hype/
Date: 2026-08-03. Read: 2 min.

A song about manufactured media narratives and who gets to write them. From It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back.

Chuck D's lyric is a media critique in the form of a hit record. The useful part for marketers is the assumption underneath it: audiences can always tell when a story is being sold to them.

### Radio Radio. Elvis Costello and the Attractions (1978)

Source: https://bravenewhive.com/songs/radio-radio/
Date: 2026-07-28. Read: 2 min.

A protest against commercial radio and the control of what gets heard. Costello famously switched to it mid-performance on Saturday Night Live in 1977.

The song is about gatekeepers deciding what reaches an audience. Replace radio with an algorithm or a model and the argument is current.
